overview: This one-page file index records October 1936 correspondence concerning the Oriental Radio Association, a possibly amateur-radio organization headquartered at Dairen in the Kwantung Leased Territory of South Manchuria. James W. Baldwin of the National Association of Broadcasters requested information after receiving an association circular announcing a winter meeting in Dairen, soliciting cooperation, and requesting QRA address cards. The Department replied that neither it nor other federal agencies possessed information and suggested consulting Kenneth Werner of the American Radio Relay League in Hartford, Connecticut.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning the Oriental Radio Association
subfiles.about: The index summarizes an inquiry from James W. Baldwin about the Dairen-based Oriental Radio Association and the Department’s response.
subfiles.summary: An October 22 entry records that James W. Baldwin of the National Association of Broadcasters requested information about the Oriental Radio Association, enclosing its circular of October 1, 1936. The circular announced a winter meeting in Dairen, requested sympathetic cooperation, and solicited QRA address cards. An October 26 reply stated that no information was available in the Department or other federal agencies, suggested that the association might consist of amateur-radio operators, and referred Baldwin to Kenneth Werner of the American Radio Relay League in Hartford.

interest: The page offers a compact record of official uncertainty about a little-known radio association operating in Japanese-controlled South Manchuria. It is useful for tracing international amateur-radio networks, the circulation of QRA cards, and American attempts to identify broadcasting organizations in the Kwantung Leased Territory. The reference to an otherwise unrepresented October 1 circular also preserves evidence of a planned Dairen meeting whose original enclosure is not present in the supplied text.
